newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to abolish Japan Development Bank--Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: Japan to abolish Japan Development Bank--Mitsuzuka.

text.p: Japan plans to abolish the Japan Development Bank (JDB), a government-affiliated institution, as part of the nation's overall administrative reform, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday.
Mitsuzuka said he came to the decision after talks with a key official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP)'s task force on administrative reform.
"I will take full responsibility for convincing ministry officials (over scrapping the JDB)," he told reporters.
Mitsuzuka said no time frame has been set yet for closing the JDB and said there were no plans at present to shift its functions to other government-affiliated institutions.
The streamlining of government-affiliated financial institutions had been at the core of discussions by the LDP's task force.
Such institutions, including the JDB and the Export-Import Bank of Japan, are overseen by the Finance Ministry.
The JDB makes long-term loans at low rates to the private sector, mainly for domestic infrastructure projects.
